hotspots.label: Seven valence electrons
hotspots.description: The small atom model shows a chlorine atom with seven outer electrons and one empty space — one electron short of a full shell.
hotspots.positionHint: The small atom model beside the samples, visible when the seven-electrons layer is on.

hotspots.label: Chloride ion (Cl⁻)
hotspots.description: When chlorine grabs one extra electron, it becomes a -1 chloride ion with a full outer shell — shown here with its new electron highlighted.
hotspots.positionHint: The small ion model beside the samples, visible when the electron-grab layer is on.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. The halogen samples float centered above a table section, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Color on the mesh is restrained: the chlorine cloud is a pale muted green, the bromine droplet a soft amber, the iodine crystal a muted violet — all desaturated, not neon. Strong saturated color is reserved entirely for the small flat hotspot dots (coral / amber / molecular green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Chlorine cloud: translucent pale green, alpha ~0.35, roughness ~0.5. Bromine droplet: soft amber, translucent (alpha ~0.8), roughness ~0.4. Iodine crystal: muted violet, matte, roughness ~0.6. Atom model: small teal electrons on translucent hairline rings. Table tiles: paper-white, roughness ~0.55. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow or pulse is handled by app runtime UI, not baked into the asset.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: the halogens shown across their states — gas, liquid, solid — plus their seven-valence-electron secret, built to be read as 'the one-electron-short family that grabs electrons.' Four procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: three samples floating at center — (a) a soft translucent pale-green cloud (several overlapping flattened spheres, alpha ~0.35) = chlorine gas, (b) a smooth amber droplet (slightly flattened sphere, alpha ~0.8) = bromine liquid, and (c) a small muted-violet crystal cluster (2-3 intergrown cubes) = iodine solid. All muted.

2) SEVEN ELECTRONS (toggleable layer): a small atom model floats beside the samples — an inner translucent ring with 2 teal electrons and an outer ring with exactly 7 teal electrons, with one small empty notch marker where an 8th would sit.

3) ELECTRON GRAB (toggleable layer): beside the atom model, a second small ion model appears — the same outer ring now holding a full 8 electrons with the newest one slightly brightened — the -1 chloride ion. A thin dashed arc connects the empty notch to the new electron (the app animates the grab).

4) GROUP 17 ON TABLE (toggleable layer): below, a flat section of periodic table (paper-white tiles, ~9 x 5). The second-to-last column is given a faint muted warm-coral cast and slight raise — Group 17.

Camera: framed so the samples are large and centered with the table slab below; auto-rotate default. Budget 8-12k triangles. Named nodes: ChlorineCloud, BromineDroplet, IodineCrystal, ShellAtom, InnerElectrons, ValenceElectrons_7, NotchMarker, ChlorideIon, GrabbedElectron, GrabArc, TableSlab, Group17Column. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer; no text on the mesh.
